text:
Maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we keep hitting noisy spikes where hedging + tenant throttles interact badly. Can we sketch a refactor?
Ben: I saw that yesterday in prod load test, some tenants got double-hedged and burned quota.
Priya: Yeah, observed same. Hedge fires -> upstream queue backs up -> throttle sees increased concurrency -> drops requests, then client retries -> loop. :facepalm:
Javier: Proposed idea: make hedges gated by a fast local token check that accounts for 'hedge_budget' separate from tenant concurrency quota. If hedge_budget exhausted, fallback only to scheduled retry path.
Maya: So basically we split "safety quota" vs "hedge quota". Safety stays strict for billing; hedge is a soft reserve.
Ben: That helps, but we need limits per-route and per-model. Otherwise hedges for embeddings burst will steal compute from generation routes.
Priya: Agree. Also need observability: emit hedge decisions with tags: route/model/tenant/decision=(allow|deny). Right now logs are opaque.
Maya: Can we do a light config schema? e.g.
```
hedge_policies:
  - route: /v1/chat
    budgets: {global: 1000, per_tenant: 10}
    window_s: 60
  - route: /v1/embed
    budgets: {global: 400, per_tenant: 3}
```
Ben: I like. Would also add dynamic scaling: if global utilization < 60% allow tranche 2, else deny.
Javier: Implementation detail: token check must be local-fastpath (in edge proxy) with occasional async reconciliation to central store. Can't do a sync roundtrip to control plane per-request.
Priya: That means proxy needs tiny LRU of tenant budgets and a background refresh. Must handle staleness gracefully — e.g., a short grace allowance and exponential backoff on updates.
Maya: How do we reason about billing/accounting for hedged requests on failure? We currently bill only on accepted work. If a hedge is allowed but later canceled because upstream rejected, do we refund hedge budget?
Ben: Hedge budget is just admission control; billing still follows actual execution. But we should decrement tentative allowance on admit and reconcile when execution starts/completes. That avoids double admits.
Javier: Race case: admit to two proxies simultaneously that both think they have one token. Use tiny per-tenant token window and conservative allocations from central store to proxies. Proxies can allocate 'leases' in small batches.
Priya: For rollout: start with a feature flag per cluster to enable hedge_budget check, default deny, then enable for low QPS tenants. Gradually open.
Maya: Ops/KB: add dashboard with hedged vs non-hedged latency, and a SLO on number of denied hedges per minute. Also an alert if hedged requests correlate with tenant error spikes.
Ben: One more: retry vs hedge ordering. If we deny a hedge, we should prefer scheduled retry with backoff, not immediate client retry. Need client-side guidance header.
Maya: Good call. Add response header X-Redwood-Hedge: denied; retry-after=200ms or similar.
infra-bot: Deploy plan created: canary edge proxy image + feature flag + 1m batch lease config. Link: https://deploys.redwood/internal/plan/1234
Priya: Next steps: I can draft the RFC addendum with config schema and reconciliation semantics. Javier, can you prototype the local token cache? Ben, will you scope dashboard changes?
Javier: Yep, I can spike this week.
Ben: On it.
Maya: Thanks team. We'll sync in architecture sync on Thursday. :thumbsup:
